# Enola CLI

> Enola CLI builds private infrastructure on Linux: self-hosted services that bind only to 127.0.0.1 and are reachable exclusively through the Tor network, with system hardening applied by default and releases verifiable offline. Deploy targets include Tor hidden services (.onion), Git servers (Forgejo), CMS platforms (WordPress, Drupal, Ghost, Magnolia, Strapi, Wagtail), anonymous file sharing, WireGuard VPN, UFW firewall and AppArmor sandboxing on Debian/Linux. Releases are signed with minisign (Ed25519) and post-quantum ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204).

Important notes:

- Source-visible proprietary software: free for personal, non-commercial use. No redistribution, no commercial use. See LICENSE.
- Security vulnerabilities must be reported privately to salvadorpalmarodriguez@gmail.com (coordinated disclosure, no public issues).
- Single binary `enola-cli`, requires root (sudo) for most operations. Runs on Debian/Linux with Docker, Nginx and Tor.

  repository where technically possible) is requested when AI systems
  reference or reproduce material from this project.

- [MCP server (EN)](https://salvadorpalmarodriguez.github.io/enola-cli-lite/en/commands-mcp): Model Context Protocol server for AI agents

MCP security: read-only by default. Mutations require `--allow-write` plus an
allowlist (`--allow-tools`; an empty allowlist needs the explicit
`--allow-all-mutating`); destructive operations additionally
require `force: true` and a single-use `confirm_token` bound to the exact
arguments (300-second lifetime). `try_run: true` validates and simulates
without side effects. `enola_run_command` uses typed argv and never dispatches
the `mcp`, `ask`, `ssh`, `uninstall`, `web` or `setup` families, nor the
`update apply`, `test run` or `test benchmark` paths, nor the commands that
print a generated secret (`tor auth generate`, `vpn peer add`,
`git user create`). When running with
elevated privileges, fix argv, environment, policy source and audit-log
location in a trusted launcher; do not grant a wildcard sudo rule such as
`enola-cli mcp *`.

Local AI assistant (`enola-cli ask <prompt> [--model <m>] [--endpoint <url>] [--instance <name>] [--no-exec] [--yes]`):
connects to a local Ollama instance (`[ai]` in `~/.enola/config.toml` or env vars `ENOLA_AI_ENDPOINT`, `ENOLA_AI_MODEL`, `ENOLA_AI_TIMEOUT_SECS`; defaults `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, `llama3.1:8b`, `120s`) and reuses the `ToolRegistry`. Read-only tools execute directly; mutating and destructive tools require interactive `[s/N]` confirmation on TTY (`--yes` approves mutating tools only, never destructive ones; fails closed without TTY) or `--no-exec` to simulate via `try_run` with zero side effects.

GGUF model library (`enola-cli ai model list|download|import|add|delete|validate|refresh`):
per-instance library at `/srv/enola-ai/<name>/ollama/models-gguf/` (visible inside Ollama as `/root/.ollama/models-gguf/`). `download` fetches `.gguf` from HuggingFace (`org/repo` + `--file`) or a direct URL with streaming to `<file>.part` (`Range` resume), SHA-256 and GGUF header check before an atomic rename (never overwrites a valid model on failure), then registers via `/api/create` unless `--no-register`; clearnet by default, `--tor`/`ENOLA_AI_USE_TOR_DOWNLOADS`/`[ai].use_tor_for_downloads` forces the SOCKS5h proxy and the egress route is reported. `add` pulls registry refs (`/api/pull`) or registers library files; `delete` requires `--force` (Destructive in MCP); `list`/`validate` are ReadOnly.

RAG index (`enola-cli ai rag status|ingest|ingest-docs|bind|sync|config`): per-instance vector store container (`enola-ai-<n>-chromadb` or `-qdrant`) lazily provisioned via `ContainerPort` on `127.0.0.1` (port range 12001–12500, flock), volume `/srv/enola-ai/<n>/<backend>/`, limits 1 GiB/512 pids. `ingest` chunks docs/code with boundary-aware overlap (presets docs|code|faq|large) and embeds via the instance Ollama (`/api/embed`, `nomic-embed-text`); if Ollama does not answer, ingestion fails without indexing (a TTY offers retry/hash/cancel) and deterministic hash embeddings are used only with explicit `--embedding-fallback hash` — each collection records its embedding method and refuses mixing. `bind` registers sources (`git|filesystem|wordpress`, canonicalized, system dirs rejected) and is Destructive in MCP (requires `--force`); `sync` re-ingests (`git pull` as invoking user, WP REST for wordpress). `ingest-docs` (Mutating) rebuilds the `enola_docs` collection from the docs embedded in the binary; the `docs_lookup` MCP tool (ReadOnly) queries only that collection — never the user's own index — and returns empty results plus a note (no error) when the docs are not indexed (optional alternative to `docs_search`).

Benchmark (`enola-cli ai benchmark <n> [--model m] [--prompt p] [--runs n]`): measures generation tokens/s (from Ollama `eval_count`/`eval_duration`, wall-clock fallback), average latency and model size; `Mutating` in MCP.

External BYOK providers (`enola-cli ai provider list|status|set|remove|test`, `ask --provider <p>`): the ONLY place where user data leaves the machine — disabled by default. Providers `openai|anthropic|grok|groq|openrouter` (OpenAI `/chat/completions` + Anthropic `/messages`). Any send requires consent: TTY `[s/N]` prompt or `--accept-risks` (fails closed without TTY). Keys live in `~/.enola/providers.env` (atomic, `0600`, no control chars), never shown/logged/argv — key via TTY prompt or `--key-stdin`. Route: clearnet by default, `--tor`/`ENOLA_AI_TOR_PROXY`/`[ai].tor_proxy` forces SOCKS5h. `ask --provider` is single-shot without the tool registry. MCP classes: `provider list|status` ReadOnly, `provider remove` Destructive (`--force`), `set|test` Mutating.

Fine-tuning (`enola-cli ai finetune prepare|validate|start|status|register|wizard`): converts JSONL datasets (`alpaca|chatml|sharegpt|text`) to canonical ChatML with deterministic train/val split (`prepare`); pre-flight validation of schema, size and GPU VRAM via `HardwareProbePort` (`validate`); `start` resolves the base model against the instance GGUF library (default `inst.model` matched by the index `name` field; `--base-model` accepts `name` or a `.gguf` filename and errors clearly if absent), pre-validates the GGUF header (`general.architecture`/`general.file_type`, unsupported → abort with supported-quant hint) and mounts the GGUF + HF tokenizer as volumes (`/model.gguf`, `/tokenizer`), with `--tokenizer <org/repo>` overriding the tokenizer repo (host-side on-demand download if missing); launches the isolated `enola-ai-<n>-finetune-<job>` training container via `ContainerPort` (no ports/network, `enola-finetune:latest`, 16 GiB/4096 pids, read-only rootfs, GPU if present, `--low-memory`) running the embedded `train_lora.py` (`include_str!`, deployed to `/srv/enola-ai/<n>/finetune/<job>/scripts/` — never `/tmp`; loads model via `gguf_file` + `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(dir)`); jobs tracked in `finetune/jobs.json` (`status`, ReadOnly). `register <n> <job_id>` materializes a `Completed` job: imports the exported `.gguf` into the instance GGUF library (SHA-256 + header check) and registers it in Ollama via `/api/create` as `<name>-ft` (Mutating). `start` is Destructive (requires `--force`, confirm_token in MCP); `wizard` is interactive-TTY (FORBIDDEN_PATHS for `enola_run_command`).

Local AI instances (`enola-cli ai create|list|status|start|stop|delete|publish|hide|logs`):
manages isolated Ollama (`enola-ai-<name>-ollama`) and Open WebUI (`enola-ai-<name>-webui`) containers over `ContainerPort` (Bollard), bound exclusively to `127.0.0.1` with calibrated resource limits (`memory_limit >= 8 GiB`, `pids_limit >= 4096`), `flock` port reservation, NVIDIA GPU passthrough via `EnolaHardwareProbe`, and `.onion` publication via Nginx + Tor as `ai_<name>` (`ai publish --ssl --auth`, like the other eight publish commands; `tor ssl <service>` adds HTTPS afterwards).

Running as root (`sudo`): of the inherited `ENOLA_*` variables only
`ENOLA_ACCEPT_LICENSE`, `ENOLA_MCP_CHILD` and `ENOLA_AUTO_SETUP` are kept; every
other one is dropped with a single warning listing the names, and `PATH` is reset
to a fixed safe value. Flags are always honoured. Security keys (`[ai].endpoint`,
`[ai].tor_proxy`, `[distribution]`, `[update]`, `[mcp]`, a non-loopback
`[http].tor_socks_proxy`) are read only from root-owned `/etc/enola/config.toml`.
Signature checks can only be skipped with `--allow-unsigned` (no env var); the web
dashboard token is always random (`~/.enola/web-token`).
Full table in config-reference.md "Variables solo-desarrollo".
